labs.title: Reaction time and the speed–accuracy trade-off
labs.protocol: Run randomized speed versus accuracy instructions in a simple choice-response task. Record accuracy and response time, inspect practice effects, and compare within-person conditions.
labs.deliverable: Guided 2–3-page report; raw data, one figure, and a conclusion.

labs.title: Psychophysics: detection and response criterion
labs.protocol: Compare detection of low-contrast targets at several strengths. Separate sensitivity from willingness to report a target and explain false alarms.
labs.deliverable: Threshold/detection results with a labeled figure and a short report.

labs.title: Selective attention and Stroop interference
labs.protocol: Counterbalance congruent and incongruent trials. Analyze response-time and accuracy differences, language familiarity, and order effects.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page experimental report. Monday sections use an equivalent asynchronous task September 7–10.

labs.title: Learning and reversal of action–outcome contingencies
labs.protocol: Use neutral stimuli and points in a browser task. Change reward contingencies, measure learning and reversal, and distinguish reinforcement from punishment.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report with learning curves; no aversive stimuli or monetary stakes.

labs.title: Working-memory load and distraction
labs.protocol: Manipulate memory load and a neutral distractor. Counterbalance conditions and compare recall accuracy without treating scores as an intelligence test.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report explaining load, interference, and design limitations.

labs.title: Memory reconstruction and source monitoring
labs.protocol: Compare neutral word-list or source-memory conditions; distinguish a recognition error from a confident claim about a personal event. Debrief fully.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report. Extended deadline avoids the Fall Recess weekend.

labs.title: Framing and risky decisions
labs.protocol: Randomize equivalent gain/loss frames using hypothetical choices. Compare choices while holding outcomes and probabilities constant.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report separating a framing effect from different underlying options.

labs.title: Infant cognition through looking-time data
labs.protocol: Analyze an instructor-provided deidentified published looking-time dataset or approved research recordings. Compare conditions and consider alternative explanations.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page data report; no infant recruitment or collection of child data.

labs.title: Personality measurement and the role of situations
labs.protocol: Use a provided deidentified item-response dataset and structured behavioral vignettes. Examine reliability, score distributions, and changes across contexts.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report; no required personal inventory or diagnostic interpretation.

labs.title: Cooperation, social norms, and group decisions
labs.protocol: Compare anonymous hypothetical contribution choices under transparent information conditions. Distinguish individual decisions from group averages.
labs.deliverable: 3–4-page report. Thursday sections use an equivalent task November 8–10 or 12; no required work November 11.

methods_assignments.title: From responses to evidence
methods_assignments.task: Clean a supplied reaction-time file; justify an exclusion rule, calculate condition summaries, and create an accurately labeled figure. Submit the editable analysis and a one-page interpretation.

methods_assignments.title: Design a fair psychological experiment
methods_assignments.task: Specify a question, variables, randomization or counterbalancing, comparison condition, ethical safeguards, and an analysis plan. Diagnose a confound in a supplied design. Submit two pages.

methods_assignments.title: Replication, uncertainty, and generalization
methods_assignments.task: Compare two supplied study summaries and datasets. Estimate and interpret a condition difference, examine uncertainty using a provided analysis template, and propose a justified follow-up. Submit the editable analysis and two pages.

notes: Separate lab sections meet Tuesday–Thursday in NEU LAB1A. Week 11 includes the individual experimental practical and mini-replication proposal support. No separate attendance or participation grade. No required lab meetings on university holidays.

options.title: Reaction time and the speed–accuracy trade-off
options.skills: Compare speed-focused and accuracy-focused instructions; summarize reaction times and errors and interpret the trade-off.

options.title: Psychophysics and signal detection
options.skills: Distinguish signal and noise trials, classify hits and false alarms, and interpret sensitivity and response criterion using the methods taught in Lab 2.

options.title: Selective attention and Stroop interference
options.skills: Compare congruent and incongruent trials; calculate interference and interpret reaction time alongside accuracy.

options.title: Working memory and distraction
options.skills: Compare memory-load and distraction conditions; calculate accuracy and interpret the effects and limitations of the design.

options.title: Memory reconstruction and source monitoring
options.skills: Follow the standardized memory procedure; distinguish recognition from source errors and interpret the findings.
